messages.subject: Replication rollback

messages.author: 0f5b7adb7e70bd8b
messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] Replication rollback
parts: Hi,
On Thu, 23 Jun 2022 at 17:50, tor son <tors...@gmail.com> wrote:

Hi,
 I am trying to repeat an activity by rollback a certain number of times, if activated. But the whole process should be repeated only a fixed number of times. For example, in total the activity should be repeated 10 times (= "remaining_replication" at the beginning). The "remaining_replication" was defined at the beginning as =-10, as it is only possible to sum up within the setting function. Each time the function is activated, the activity is repeated 3 times. But for the fourth activation of the function, the activity shall be repeated only once, to have in total 10 replications. I tried to set a new attribute in two different options, but this does not work. The function is part of several connected functions.

Note that the "times" parameter is a fixed number. If you need more complex rollbacks, you may use the "check" argument. But in this case, since (from your description, I assume) you are placing different arrivals in that trajectory using the activate() activity, I would use a simple fixed rollback, and then a leave() activity on top, controlled by a global like this:

library(simmer)

work <- trajectory() %>%
  leave(function() get_global(env, "work_repeats") == 0) %>%
  log_("doing something") %>%
  timeout(1) %>%
  set_global("work_repeats", -1, mod="+") %>%
  rollback(4, times=2) %>%
  log_("done") %>%
  activate("work")

env <- simmer() %>%
  add_generator("init", work, at(0)) %>%
  add_generator("work", work, when_activated()) %>%
  add_global("work_repeats", 10)

run(env)
#> 0: init0: doing something
#> 1: init0: doing something
#> 2: init0: doing something
#> 3: init0: done
#> 3: work0: doing something
#> 4: work0: doing something
#> 5: work0: doing something
#> 6: work0: done
#> 6: work1: doing something
#> 7: work1: doing something
#> 8: work1: doing something
#> 9: work1: done
#> 9: work2: doing something
#> simmer environment: anonymous | now: 10 | next: 
#> { Monitor: in memory }
#> { Source: init | monitored: 1 | n_generated: 1 }
#> { Source: work | monitored: 1 | n_generated: 3 }
#> { Global: work_repeats | schedule: FALSE | initial value: 10 }
Hope it helps,
Iñaki

work_func <-function (name, envs,
                      usual_replication,
                      activate_next){
 
  name<-trajectory("name")%>%
   
   
    set_global("delivery", 1, mod="+")%>%  
   
    seize("resource", 1) %>%
   
 
    #option 1
    set_attribute("replication ", function() min (usual_replication, -1*get_global(envs, "remaining_replication")))%>%
   
    #option 2
    set_attribute (" replication   ", function ()
      ifelse (get_global(envs, " remaining_replication  ")*-1 <   usual_replication  , get_global(envs, " remaining_replication  ")*-1,  usual_replication  )) %>%
   
   
   
    log_("activity")%>%
    timeout(function() rnorm (1, 10, 0)) %>%  
   
    rollback(2, get_attribute(envs, "replication")) %>%  
   
    set_global("remaining_replication",  function() min (usual_replication, -1*get_global(envs, "remaining_replication"))), mod="+")%>%
 
 
    release("resource", 1) %>%
 
    log_(function() paste("Delivery:", get_global(envs, "delivery"), "finished")) %>%
 
    activate (activate_next)

}

messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] Replication rollback
parts:
Thanks for the quick reply. Yes, your assumptions are right. But one important point I should have mentioned is that at the end the activate (activate_next) function should be executed. This cannot be done by the leave function and the leave function will set the finished as FALSE, as far as I understand it right. So this would be a simplified example.

library(simmer)

start <- trajectory() %>%
  log_("start")%>%
  activate("work")

work <- trajectory() %>%
  leave(function() get_global(env, "work_repeats") == 0) %>%
  log_("doing something") %>%
  timeout(1) %>%
  set_global("work_repeats", -1, mod="+") %>%
  rollback(4, times=2) %>%
  log_("done") %>%

activate("finish")

finish <- trajectory() %>%
  batch (4) %>%
  log_("finsih")
env <- simmer() %>%
add_generator("init", start, at (0,10, 20, 30)) %>%
add_generator("work", work, when_activated()) %>%
add_generator("finish", finish, when_activated()) %>%

add_global("work_repeats", 10)

run(env)
